data.title: Rejection naming a specific industry sector as required
data.content:
# Rejection naming a specific industry sector as required

The stated reason is the absence of experience in one named sector, rather than the depth or correctness of the work assessed.

### Diagnostic Non-Inferences
- Does not establish that the sector was irrelevant to the work.
- Does not establish that the assessed work fell short in any respect.
data.summary: The stated reason is the absence of experience in one named sector, rather than the depth or correctness of the work assessed.

probes.action: Compare the sector named in the message against the requirements section of the posting as it stood on the day of application.
probes.expected_signal: Establishes whether the sector was listed as required, listed as preferred, or absent.

outcomes.label: The posting named the sector among the requirements.
outcomes.because: An explicit requirement stated up front weighs against the claim that the domain criterion was introduced only after assessment began.

outcomes.label: The posting named the sector, among preferences or nice-to-haves rather than requirements.
The posting did not mention the sector at all.
outcomes.because: An unmentioned sector criterion makes post-hoc goalpost shifting more plausible than evaluation solely against published standards.

outcomes.label: No copy of the posting as applied to was kept.

specimens.label: Feedback after the technical round
specimens.subject: Following your technical session

lines.text: The exercise was solid and the reasoning about failure modes was strong.
The team decided to go with someone who has already worked in the payments domain.
We would be happy to talk again for a role where that is less central.

specimens.reading: The work is assessed positively and the ground for the decision is elsewhere. That combination is what makes the sector legible as the operative line — and leaves open how heavily it was weighed.

perspectives.sees: A reason that names an industry rather than a capability: payments, health, advertising, trading — a sector the candidate has not worked in, stated as the thing that was missing.
perspectives.reads: The sector is a real difference. Whether it is a difference in what the work requires, or a proxy standing in for that, the message does not distinguish — and the two look identical from outside.
perspectives.does: Compares the sector named against the requirements the posting listed, because a requirement that appears only in the closing message appeared somewhere between the two.

perspectives.sees: Two candidates who can both build the system, one of whom has already met the constraints this sector imposes and will not spend the first quarter discovering them.
perspectives.reads: Sector context is a real cost, paid in ramp-up time that the team carries. Weighing it is judgement, not a rule, and nothing in the process asks how much of it was weighed.
perspectives.does: States the difference plainly, because it is the most concrete thing that separated two people who both passed.

perspectives.sees: A requirement that was written into the search brief as a preference and is now being applied as a threshold.
perspectives.reads: Preferences and thresholds are recorded in the same field. Which one a line was is decided when it is used, not when it is written.
perspectives.does: Passes the reason on in the manager's words, because it is specific enough to send and not attributable to anything the recruiter assessed.

non_inferences: Does not establish that the sector was irrelevant to the work.
Does not establish that the assessed work fell short in any respect.
